lines.text: OpenAI and Cisco made a temporary shield for servers waiting on a patch.
Patching can take days or weeks. Blocking an action outright could also break normal requests.
lines.title: The problem

lines.text: Shirudo uses eBPF, which runs tiny, checked programs inside the Linux core.
lines.title: Key idea

lines.text: A shield is tested first, approved by an operator, then loaded without restarting.
lines.title: How it works

lines.text: Shields are signed and checked, and a hardware chip keeps a record of what was loaded.
lines.title: Trust

lines.text: In a test, a shield made by Codex blocked an attack on Elasticsearch, which kept running.
lines.title: The test

lines.text: The takeaway: protect the gap between finding a bug and patching it.
